transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Leo Chan (Redwood); Marta Ruiz, Samir Patel, Evan Cho, Nina Gomez, Alex Zhao (BrightLayer)

Auto-generated summary: (may be noisy) Reviewed TTFT metrics + streaming. Action items listed separately.

00:00 Jordan Lee: okay everyone, hi, thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly POC sync for BrightLayer, good to see you all. quick roll call?
00:08 Marta Ruiz: Marta here.
00:10 Samir Patel: Samir.
00:11 Evan Cho: Evan.
00:12 Nina Gomez: Nina.
00:14 Jordan Lee: great, thanks. Priya and Leo from our side? Priya: you want to intro real quick.
00:19 Priya Nair: hey all, Priya, SE on inference perf. I'll run through the microbench numbers first then we'll go into kernel and streaming tradeoffs.
00:29 Jordan Lee: quick agenda: TTFT numbers, streaming chunk sizes, sequence length sim, kernel choices, open Qs, next steps.
00:36 Samir Patel: mostly interested in TTFT at 2k and 4k, and how streaming interacts with KV cache. also we saw weird p99 spikes last week.
00:45 Priya Nair: yep we'll address p99. note these numbers are from our baseline harness, there might be small transcription differences vs your harness.
00:53 02:10 Priya Nair: okay slide-free: latest run, single-stream request path (no streaming) on 2k seq, model trimmed to 7B, quantized to 4-bit. median first token (TTFT) was 42ms, p95 120ms, p99 210ms. when we enable streaming with 128B chunks TTFT goes to 60ms median, p95 160ms. so streaming added some overhead for initial token due to chunk handshake and flush.
02:45 Samir Patel: wait, streaming added overhead? we were expecting streaming to help first token by starting earlier.
02:52 Priya Nair: good question — depends on how the runtime does prefix/KV warmup. our streaming pipeline currently waits to assemble the first chunk and populate the KV cache up to the first attention window; that can add a couple of tens of ms. when using very small chunks like 32-64B it's better for perceived prompt streaming but can increase overhead on GPU kernel launch frequency.
03:21 Evan Cho: are these runs with continuous batching? we saw batching artifacts when we ran concurrent users.
03:26 Priya Nair: these are single-tenant synthetic runs, no batching. for concurrency we see different p95s because of batching and kernel fusion.
03:40 05:00 Leo Chan: also remember kernel choice matters: Triton kernels we used yield slightly lower p50 but higher p95 in some cases due to kernel launch variance; TVM showed flatter tails for our 4k experiments. but depends on model shape and sequence distribution.
05:28 Marta Ruiz: hmm, curious about TVM vs Triton — we thought Triton was more mature for these 7B models. is Redwood running custom kernels?
05:36 Priya Nair: we do have Redwood-optimized kernels that pick different code paths depending on seq length. that's the "redwood runt" in the notes, sometimes transcribed as rewood runt. they handle KV cache streaming more aggressively. but it's a tradeoff: custom paths can reduce latency for typical seq lengths but may degrade for rare long sequences.
06:02 Samir Patel: about p99 spikes — can you point to root cause? last week we saw p99 jump to 400ms on 2k sequences.
06:12 Priya Nair: we traced those to sporadic CPU-side GC in the orchestrator plus occasional kernel eviction when the GPU ran out of reserved buffer for KV cache. in one run there was a tails effect from concurrent microbatching. we'll share flame graphs.
06:30 Nina Gomez: on security side, if you folks are suggesting dedicated capacity or private deployment we need KMS integration details and audit log retention info.
06:40 Jordan Lee: yes, we'll send the SOC2 pack and KMS notes after the call; Priya will loop in the security docs.
06:46 08:00 Samir Patel: can you explain sequence length tradeoffs? we plan to push some flows to 4k and some remain 2k. how does kernel selection behave?
08:10 Priya Nair: very briefly: many kernels are optimized for a particular max sequence window. if you mostly run 2k, choosing code paths tuned for 2k gives best p50 and p95. for mixed workloads the runtime can route requests to a compatible model variant with a different compilation profile — that introduces routing overhead but keeps tail latency predictable.
08:40 Leo Chan: also quantization effects: 4-bit q can be slightly faster but may increase compute variance depending on GEMM scheduling on the kernel.
08:52 Alex Zhao: can we hybridize — like 2k for most but fall back to a 4k variant only when longer input detected?
08:58 Priya Nair: exactly, we recommend that for BrightLayer: pin most traffic to a 2k-optimized variant and use a fallback 4k variant with a small traffic percentage or explicit routing on request metadata. that preserves TTFT for the majority.
09:15 12:30 Samir Patel: about streaming config: what chunk sizes do you recommend for lower perceived latency without hurting p99?
12:36 Priya Nair: empirically 64-128B is a good starting point. 32B can increase kernel launches and overhead; 256B reduces initial interactivity. we saw best balance at 96/128B in our tests. but your decoder tokens are slightly larger due to tokenization differences so we'll share tuned values.
12:58 Marta Ruiz: interesting. we need real numbers on our infra. Evan, can you run the Triton vs TVM microbench with our 4k workload?
13:08 Evan Cho: yes I can but need the harness and expected env vars.
13:12 Priya Nair: we'll push the harness (docker + run script) to your S3 bucket; it's lightweight. it includes a small client that can simulate streaming vs non-streaming.
13:20 18:00 Samir Patel: what about KV cache memory pressure — any knobs to reduce eviction? we had evictions when many concurrent sessions warmed large context windows.
18:12 Priya Nair: a few levers: increase reserved KV buffer per instance (cost), reduce per-request warmed context by lazy caching, or enable prefix sharing for identical prompts. also we have a policy to evict LRU across microbatches; we can tune eviction thresholds. We'll propose specific configs in the doc.
18:40 Jordan Lee: quick question from sales side: any blockers on Dedicated vs Hosted for you?
18:46 Marta Ruiz: security is the main one, plus cost predictability. Dedicated with reserved GPUs looks promising but we need SSO + audit logs and data residency noted.
18:58 Nina Gomez: yes, and encryption-at-rest with a customer-managed KMS would be required for our on-prem pilot.
19:05 Jordan Lee: noted, we'll supply KMS integration guide and SOC2 artifacts.
19:10 24:00 Alex Zhao: curious about fallback routing. if 2k variant is down do you auto-fallback to hosted? what's the fail-open behavior?
24:10 Priya Nair: Redwood runtime supports policies: canary, automatic fallback to a compatible variant or region, or return an error if strict. for your pilot we'd probably suggest canary then auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant then to hosted as last resort depending on SLO.
24:35 Samir Patel: can we get a run that simulates failover to measure impact?
24:40 Priya Nair: yes we can run a controlled failover during a canary slot.
24:48 Jordan Lee: action item: schedule a 30-minute canary with simulated failover during low-traffic window.
24:56 32:00 Priya Nair: quick note on telemetry: please send us the sample prompts distribution. we need token-length histogram to pick chunk sizes and select kernel profiles.
32:10 Samir Patel: we'll export a one-week anonymized histogram.
32:18 Evan Cho: also I'll share our infra spec: A100 80GB, NVLink, 100GbE, driver 535.
32:25 Priya Nair: perfect, that helps.
32:30 38:00 Marta Ruiz: any blockers on model variant management? we want to be able to pin versions per route.
38:06 Leo Chan: Redwood console supports per-route pinning, canary traffic splits and automatic rollbacks. we'll show a demo if helpful.
38:20 Marta Ruiz: yes please, schedule a short demo.
38:25 Jordan Lee: will do.
38:30 44:00 Nina Gomez: follow-up on compliance: can you confirm audit log retention options and whether logs can go to our SIEM?
44:10 Jordan Lee: yes, we support log export to Kafka/S3 and we can push to a SIEM via connectors; retention configurable. we'll send a diagram.
44:22 Nina Gomez: great.
44:30 49:00 Jordan Lee: okay to recap: Redwood will share microbench harness and logs, security pack, propose canary slots. BrightLayer will run kernel microbench and send token histograms and infra baseline. we agreed on chunk 64-128B starting point and fallback strategy to 4k variant. action items recorded.
49:20 Marta Ruiz: sounds good, thanks.
49:25 Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with calendar invites.
49:30 Meeting ends.
